description: UK: can I retire at 60 with £300k (or any age and pot)? Year by year to 95 for one person or a couple, on the 2027-28 rules after Budget 2026: pay and pension contributions until retirement, pots drawn from the normal minimum pension age (55, 57 from 6 April 2028) with 25% tax-free cash within the £268,275 Lump Sum Allowance and the rest drawn as taxable income, defined benefit pensions, the new State Pension from the State Pension age by date of birth (full £250.70 a week from April 2027), savings, a spending target in today’s money, and income tax (personal allowance tapered over £100,000; England/Wales/NI or Scottish bands, frozen to 2030-31) and National Insurance on pay. Growth and inflation are assumptions. Returns the age the money lasts to, bridge years, wealth at retirement, the spending that lasts to 95, a retire-at-60/62/65 comparison and key years in today’s money.
